newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Scania says new trucks dent profit.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Scania says new trucks dent profit.

text.p: Swedish truck and bus maker Scania said Thursday its profits dropped 39 percent in the first nine months of the year, blaming the stronger Swedisn crown, a restructuring programme and the cost of its new 4-series trucks.

Scania posted a profit of 2.14 billion crowns ($324 million) after financial items, down from 3.51 billion ($531 million) in the same 1995 period. Sales totalled 24.57 billion ($3.7 billion) crowns for the period compared with 25.44 billion ($3.8 billion).
If sales had been adjusted for the strength of the Swedish crown, they would have risen two percent, Scania said.
The stronger currency was also to blame for 720 million crowns ($109 million) of the nine-month profit slide, but that was not the only reason, Scania said.
Costs incurred in the changeover in European production to the group's new 4-series trucks from the older 3-series had also been a serious drain.
The profit came in well short of market expectations, and by the close Scania shares were 9 crowns ($1.35) lower at 167 ($25.30).
